pairs.why: A matches the real umbrella's soft, scalloped, rib-free canopy, while B's exposed ribs, hub hardware and glossier panels make it a different, more mechanical build.
Both canopies are built right, but A has a slightly more matte, calmer finish, while B has brighter specular highlights and a thicker, shinier pole.
A fills the frame like the real card, with big chunky ice cubes and the straw inside the glass, while B is a small, photoreal glass with tiny ice that doesn't read as this game's illustration.
A's tall straight glass, diagonal straw through the juice and frame-filling scale follow the real card closely, while B is undersized and more photographic.
A has the real card's big cubes and illustrated scale but is overglossed and toy-like, while B is calmer but small and photoreal, so A is only slightly closer.
B's glossy plastic hot-pink branches on neon green read as a toy, while A is busier than the real card but keeps its matte, dotted, calmer-coloured coral.
The two are nearly identical builds, but B's darker, calmer green background and slightly softer saturation sit closer to the real card than A's brighter, punchier palette.
B has the deeper, calmer green and slightly more matte coral of the real card, while A's background is washed light and its pinks are a bit more saturated.
